- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early days of the 30d horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is falling sharply.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 75+), especially in days with high sentiment; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon: if forecast is >75, reduce by 2–5% per day if sentiment is flat or negative; if <70, increase by 1–3% if sentiment is positive.
- Forecast bias is strongest in first 5–7 days of 30d horizon — adjust downward if sentiment is weak or mixed.
- If sentiment is consistently 0.00, model tends to drift toward historical mean; use 30d moving average as baseline for correction.
